key_insight: QAOA mixer design faces two complementary bottlenecks: probability transport across configurations and finite-depth causal reach across the problem graph.
engineering_relevance: Problem-aligned two-local mixers can improve shallow-circuit approximation ratios, but greater causal reach alone does not guarantee better performance.
method: Derive small-angle objective bounds linked by a graph-Laplacian identity.
Bound achievable concentration using layer-wise mixer-unitary spreading.
Evaluate X+XX and X+YY mixers for MaxCut, with causal radius at most 2p at depth p.
evidence_signal: Across cycles, circular ladders, and high-girth regular bipartite graphs, augmented mixers improved best-found ratios at equal depth; X+YY at depth p came within about one approximation-ratio point of X at depth 2p in examined reach-matched cases.
watch_item: Results concern best-found numerical performance on selected graph families, not guaranteed gains or hardware-level resource savings.
paper_title: Structural Bottlenecks in QAOA Mixer Design: Transport and Causal Reach
